messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 SEV2: Repeated container restarts on gpu-node-14/gpu-pool during prefill phase. Error rate spike 03:12–03:22 UTC, ~120 restarts detected. Symptoms: CUDA OOM in runtime prefill, pods auto-restarted. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-oom-prefill. Paging oncall: @oncall-jen

oncall-jen: I'm awake, acked. jumping in now. grabbing logs and node metrics.

runtime-alex: I see the trace in the runtime logs, sample:

```
2026-02-27T03:14:10Z ERROR runtime: kernel panic while prefill
tensorflow/llm: CUDA out of memory. tried to alloc 4.2G
stack: prefill.go:128 -> kvcache.go:45 -> cuda_kernel.cu
container restarted (OOM)
```

runtime-alex: Prefill sizes spiking — a few requests attempted prefill lengths ~16000 tokens (user long-prompt + system + context). GPU mem usage shot to 100% and kernel failed.

eng-maya: ugh, known risk with current prefill path. we haven't enforced a prefill token cap on hosted tier. short-term: can we reject/400 requests that indicate prefill > 8k tokens? also consider a soft-signal header so clients get a clear error.

oncall-jen: good call. @sre-ram can we put a global rate limit or conditional request filter at the gateway to drop prefill-heavy requests? need fix within 30 min to avoid broader degradation.

sre-ram: can do. i'll push an NGINX route rule to check header X-Prefill-Tokens (if present) and reject >8192. if header absent, fallback to size estimation by content-length. rolling patch now to edge nodes.

support-lin: logging: support queue shows a cluster of 5 customers with elevated 5xx in that window. collecting customer IDs and example request ids to attach to incident ticket.

runtime-alex: while gateway patch rolls, i'm going to deploy a runtime guard patch that fails prefill early if estimated kv-cache growth >70% of GPU mem. quick patch diff:

```
if prefill_estimated_bytes > gpu_mem * 0.7 {
  return error(413, "prefill too large: reduce prompt/context")
}
```

runtime-alex: building - will push to canary pool gpu-pool-canary-1.

sre-ram: gateway rule deployed to 6 edge nodes. started returning 429 for a small fraction of traffic matching >8k heuristic. watching for side effects.

eng-maya: note — some SDKs don't send X-Prefill-Tokens header. we should publish a breaking-safe guidance: SDKs should send token-hint header; otherwise we do best-effort estimation.

oncall-jen: canary runtime patch is up. observed canary handle prefill requests that previously OOM'd. no restarts in canary for last 6 minutes. promoting to gpu-pool-1 with 20% traffic shift.

incident-bot: update: 1845124250, automated scaling triggered on gpu-pool-1 at +2 nodes (policy: emergency-burst). helpful but not sufficient alone.

support-lin: customers affected so far: CUST-872, CUST-309 (high volume), CUST-501. approx impact window: 03:12–03:21 UTC. failure mode: requests failed with 5xx container restarts or 429/413 from temporary filters. attaching sample request ids.

cs-tom: drafting customer message: "We experienced an incident affecting long-context generation. Requests that exceeded ~8k tokens could see errors between 03:12–03:21 UTC. We've applied mitigations and are rolling a permanent fix." will send to affected Customer Success reps for review.

sre-ram: after canary looks good, rolled runtime patch to remaining pods at 03:40 UTC with controlled parallelism. pods stabilized; restarts dropped to baseline.

oncall-jen: confirmed cluster-wide pod restart rate normalized by 03:45 UTC. Metrics: restart_count back to <1/hr per node. GPU memory pressure reduced.

eng-maya: follow-up action items: 1) add prefill token limit in hosted API and SDK (owner: eng-maya) 2) improve prefill memory accounting in runtime (owner: runtime-alex) 3) add synthetic tests for long prompt prefill (owner: eng-ml) 4) document customer-facing guidance for long-context usage (owner: cs-tom).

support-lin: prepared incident ticket with customer impact details and sample IDs. will update CS and triage for credits if needed.

cs-tom: sending customer comms in 10m. will include suggested workaround: trim system messages or use chunked generation + context stitching.

oncall-jen: handing off to night oncall at 04:00 UTC. leaving remediation and follow-ups in #incidents. if anything regresses, page me.

eng-maya: postmortem requested; I'll start the doc and include timeline + root cause: lack of prefill cap + some large customer workloads + runtime prefill path lacking memory guardrails.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. root cause suspected: GPU OOM in prefill path triggered by very long context requests. next steps: postmortem + SDK/gateway tokens limit + runtime guard.

runtime-alex: logs and traces saved to /var/log/incidents/1845123456-oom-prefill.tar.gz for postmortem.

oncall-jen: thanks all. good job coordinating. (reacted :thumbsup:)
